test.//: Cap each vitest's worker pool. Nx runs `parallel` projects at once and EVERY vitest independently scales its pool to the CPU count, unaware of the others — so the pools multiply (3 projects x 6 CPUs = 18 concurrent jsdom environments). That exhausts memory: tests crawl past the 5s timeout and the OS kills the worker, which surfaces as a passing-but-non-zero-exit task that Nx then labels FLAKY. Keep (nx parallel x maxThreads) at or under the core count.

lint.//: `^production` is load-bearing: @typescript-eslint/no-deprecated is type-aware, so a project's lint result depends on its DEPENDENCIES' source (the @deprecated tag lives there). Without dependency inputs, deprecating an export in util-matrix leaves every consumer reporting a cached pass — the ban silently stops working across exactly the lib boundaries it exists to police.
